properties.name: Hou Hanshu eclipse of 31 CE — Luoyang court
properties.found: Channel claims Later Han annals record an "impossible" eclipse, the phrase "man from heaven died", and the emperor taking the people's sins on himself, around the crucifixion (dated by the video to 3 April 33).
properties.support: Hou Hanshu, Guangwu annals, Jianwu 7 (31 CE): 三月癸亥晦，日有食之 — on the last day (guihai) of the 3rd month the sun was eclipsed. On the eclipse day the emperor left the main hall and issued a self-blame edict (吾德薄致災 — my thin virtue brought this disaster). A later edict (summer, 4th month, renwu day) says: 比陰陽錯謬，日月薄食。百姓有過，在予一人 — lately yin and yang have gone wrong and the sun and moon have been eclipsed; if the people have faults, the blame is on me, the one man. It then grants a general amnesty. The Chinese date (last day of the 3rd month) matches the annular solar eclipse of 10 May 31 CE — not a Passover date and not the crucifixion darkness.
properties.notes: Rating: MISLEADING. The eclipse (a real solar eclipse, 10 May 31 CE) and the edict exist, but the date is 31 not 33; "the people's faults rest on me" is a stock formula of Chinese royal self-blame (from the Analects 20.1 堯曰 and the Shangshu), not atonement theology; the "man from heaven died" line was not found in the annals.
properties.caveat: Verify full annal text on ctext before wiring; "rainbow halo" claim not checked.

recent_updates.title: New video: 上帝 Shàngdì as an ancient Chinese name for God
recent_updates.text: The creator remembers saying 上帝 Shàngdì, the word many Chinese Protestant churches use for God, and argues that the name was used in China long before Christianity arrived. He presents this as a link to the biblical God.
recent_updates.caveat: Shangdi appears in Shang oracle bones (c. 1250–1050 BCE), mostly as 帝 Di; the full form 上帝 is common in the Shijing and Shangshu, so the “3,500 years” figure is generous. Some Christians see Shangdi as an echo of early knowledge of the one Creator; scholars see him as the high god of Shang and Zhou religion, alongside ancestor worship. This is a comparison, not the same as YHWH. 上帝 was later chosen by Protestant translators for “God” in Chinese Bibles (Catholics mostly use 天主 Tiānzhǔ), so the church word comes from that translation choice.
